proof_attempt_summary: D0 proved the signed Gaussian benchmark phase diagram, the sharp O(c²) singular value rate, an outward-rounded certificate, an unbounded overlap-to-full-bound ratio, and fixed-known-oracle ATT inference. D0.5 math review passed and both cited sources were verified. The general review rated the delivered package incremental because feasible estimated-score selection and uniform post-selection coverage across phase ties remain open; two positioning comments in review_rubric.json were not repaired before the below-floor bank. A field-tier re-raise needs a new estimated-score and tie-robust inference kernel, not another presentation pass.
tldr: For Gaussian covariates with a treatment mean shift of either alignment sign and exponential outcome heteroskedasticity, the unrestricted nonparametric ATT efficiency bound after releasing a legal scalar score has an exact one-dimensional objective with continuous-onset, interior-jump, and direct-endpoint phases plus the orthogonal branch. The minimum value approaches its orthogonal limit at the sharp \(O(Tc^2)\) rate, although sign-adjusted optimizer sets converge only graphically at a switch. The benchmark is an exact heteroskedastic slice of Clivio et al.'s published Gaussian GLM class; after verifying the extra regularity hypotheses of their Theorem 4.5, their overlap-optimal prognostic rule can be arbitrarily inefficient for this full bound for every fixed \(0<|c|<1\). Positive-tolerance certification and a cross-fitted efficient estimator give computable values and uniform studentized coverage at any fixed known oracle score, including either member of a tie.
gap: The closest paper proves that prognostic scores optimize overlap divergence and explicitly leaves optimization of the full efficiency bound open. Existing ATT efficiency papers provide the bound but do not optimize it over the legal Gaussian score continuum.
fill: An exact weighted-secant and one-valley analysis supplies the global phase diagram, branch limit, and certified computation, while benchmark-specific moment and information bounds connect the minimum to attainable fixed-oracle inference.
